sources.institution: Library of Congress Federal Research Division, historical Country Study (HTML transcription)
sources.title: Ethiopia — Gondar and the Era of Princes
sources.usage: Read entire body, especially paragraphs 16–21: late eighteenth/early nineteenth-century ceremonial emperors, autonomous provincial nobles, rival emperors around 1800. Unified effective sovereignty explicitly rejected; medieval church and modern institutions excluded.

sources.institution: Library of Congress Federal Research Division, historical Country Study (HTML transcription)
sources.title: Ethiopia — Tewodros II to Menelik II, 1855–89
sources.usage: Read body paragraphs 1–13: Yohannis IV crowned 1872, regional rivals, Menelik submission in 1878, Egyptian occupation of Harer from 1875 for nearly a decade. Exact Harer withdrawal date/governor and uniform Ethiopian central control not established.

sources.institution: Library of Congress Federal Research Division, historical Country Study (HTML transcription)
sources.title: Ethiopia — Menelik II, 1889–1913
sources.usage: Read all 17 body paragraphs: Menelik political control around 1900, Addis Ababa permanent capital in 1890s, conquest, 1896 recognition, 1907 Council of Ministers and later regency. Later ministers/regency not projected into 1900.

sources.institution: Library of Congress Federal Research Division, historical Country Study (HTML transcription)
sources.title: Ethiopia — Interregnum and Zawditu/Tafari
sources.usage: Read all body paragraphs: Menelik death 1913, uncrowned Iyasu, Zawditu as empress and Tafari regent/heir, Habte Giorgis influence until 1926, Tafari succession 1930. No precise 1916 coup day or blanket sovereign authority for a single regent claimed.

sources.institution: Library of Congress Federal Research Division, historical Country Study (HTML transcription)
sources.title: Ethiopia — Haile Selassie before the invasion
sources.usage: Read full body: Zawditu died April 1930, Haile Selassie crowned November, constitution granted July 1931 with supreme imperial powers. December 1930 and January 1932 editorial starts avoid inventing accession/coronation/promulgation days.

sources.institution: Library of Congress Federal Research Division, historical Country Study (HTML transcription)
sources.title: Ethiopia — invasion and Italian occupation
sources.usage: Read all body paragraphs: invasion 3 October 1935, Addis Ababa occupation May 1936, claimed annexation and international disagreement, East African administrative unit and continued Ethiopian resistance. Occupation is not consensual or universally recognised sovereignty.

sources.institution: Library of Congress Federal Research Division, historical Country Study (HTML transcription)
sources.title: Ethiopia — World War II and restoration
sources.usage: Read full body: emperor returned 5 May 1941, January 1942 sovereign-state agreement and reserved British zones, rebuilding imperial administration. Temporary British reserved jurisdiction distinguished from complete restoration; no unchanged 1942 advisory arrangement claimed for 1945.

sources.institution: Library of Congress Federal Research Division, historical Country Study (HTML transcription)
sources.title: Ethiopia — Administrative Change and the 1955 Constitution
sources.usage: Read entire body: enlarged ministries, imperial judiciary, revised 1955 constitution, appointed Senate and nominally elected Deputies, elite control and gap between rights and practice. Mid-1960s fourteen provinces not projected into 1960.

sources.institution: Library of Congress Federal Research Division, historical Country Study (HTML transcription)
sources.title: Ethiopia — attempted coup of December 1960
sources.usage: Read full body: coup began 13 December, capital seizure, loyalist resistance and emperor returned 17 December. Coup interval omitted from constitutional mappings; December 17 return is documented, not a guessed day.

sources.institution: Library of Congress Federal Research Division, historical Country Study (HTML transcription)
sources.title: Somalia — imperial partition
sources.usage: Read all 12 body paragraphs: northern British treaties, French protectorate, Italian southern colonial expansion/protected sultanates, Egyptian ambitions, Harer incorporation by Menelik between 1887 and 1897. Colony-wide control and consent not inferred; contradictory early Italian treaty-year simplifications not used as exact dates.

sources.institution: Library of Congress Federal Research Division, historical Country Study (HTML transcription)
sources.title: Somalia — peninsula before imperial partition
sources.usage: Read all body paragraphs: limited Omani authority on Banaadir coast, northern Mukha/Ottoman nominal tribute and local governors. This does not establish a unified Somali political state in 1815; no individual coastal framework mapped onto a generic whole.

sources.institution: Library of Congress Federal Research Division, historical Country Study (HTML transcription)
sources.title: Somalia — consolidation of colonial rule
sources.usage: Read full body: Italian governor-led administration, Carletti 1906–10 and fascist-era governor, distinction from British Somaliland. Formal governor office is supported; exact 1914/1920/1930 officeholder names, uniform control and colonial civilising claims omitted.

sources.institution: Library of Congress Federal Research Division, historical Country Study (HTML transcription)
sources.title: Somalia — dervish resistance
sources.usage: Read complete body: dervish resistance against British/Ethiopians from 1899 to 1920. British protectorate status does not imply uniform practical control; casualty estimates omitted.

sources.institution: Library of Congress Federal Research Division, historical Country Study (HTML transcription)
sources.title: Somalia — British military administration
sources.usage: Read entire body: separate northern military governor and former Italian territory military commander, no integrated Somali administration, advisory councils, international disposition and 1949 trusteeship decision. Proposed Greater Somalia and territorial rhetoric not accepted as sovereignty.

sources.institution: Library of Congress Federal Research Division, historical Country Study (HTML transcription)
sources.title: Somalia — trusteeship, protectorate and 1960 independence
sources.usage: Read all 38 body paragraphs: AFIS/UN oversight, 1956 assembly and Iise ministry, north independence 26 June and union/republic 1 July 1960, elected president/PM accountable to 123-member assembly. AFIS powers explicitly confined to earlier years where stated; 1961 referendum not retrojected.

sources.institution: Library of Congress Federal Research Division, historical Country Study (HTML transcription)
sources.title: Uganda — early political systems
sources.usage: Read body, especially Early Political Systems paragraphs 5–20: Bunyoro political state/omukama and royal clan, Buganda kabaka/chiefs and expansion. People identities, origin legends, broad archaeological claims and dated nineteenth-century statistics excluded. Narrow cores use kingship, not an unchanged constitution.

sources.institution: Library of Congress Federal Research Division, historical Country Study (HTML transcription)
sources.title: Uganda — trade, foreign contact and conquest
sources.usage: Read full body: Buganda religious civil wars from 1888, British intervention, Kabarega/Bunyoro resistance and conquest; Egyptian attempt on Bunyoro resisted. Later colonial institutions not projected into 1878/1880.

sources.institution: Library of Congress Federal Research Division, historical Country Study (HTML transcription)
sources.title: Uganda — colonial administration and kingdom agreements
sources.usage: Read all body paragraphs: 1900 commissioner and Buganda Agreement, chiefs/royal line under dependency, imposed Baganda administration in Bunyoro, removal after 1907 revolt, regional colonial differences through 1940s. Buganda agreement exact day unknown; accepted dependent Buganda core begins conservatively 1901.

sources.institution: Library of Congress Federal Research Division, historical Country Study (HTML transcription)
sources.title: Uganda — issue of independence
sources.usage: Read complete body: governor Cohen arrived 1952 and reorganised Legislative Council with African district representatives. Conservative 1953 start; no independence or 1961 responsible-government institutions in 1960.

sources.institution: Library of Congress Federal Research Division, historical Country Study (HTML transcription)
sources.title: Uganda — power politics in Buganda
sources.usage: Read entire body: 1953 exile/restoration, 1960 unresolved unitary/federal negotiations, 1961 responsible-government elections and 1962 independence. Later Obote PM and federal arrangement not copied into 1960.

sources.institution: Republic of Djibouti official historical legal archive
sources.title: Arrêté 60/40/SPCG — Territorial Assembly extraordinary session
sources.usage: Downloaded public HTML, stripped scripts/styles and read original full body: 3 June 1960 instrument cites 1957 government council/assembly legislation and 1958 assembly ordinance; territorial chief chairs government council, territorial assembly summoned for 8 June. Named Compain/Ahmed Dini office tenures not extrapolated; no 1977 republic.

sources.institution: Cambridge University Press / original archival historical research
sources.title: The Sultans of Zanzibar and the Abolition of Slavery in East Africa
sources.usage: Read historical body Writing the 1890 Decree and Anti-Slavery Policies in the Courts, including paragraphs 516–528 and 566–582: Oman division, sultans, local governors/kadhis and British pressure, 1897 judicial reforms. Full literal uniform rule or successful abolition not assumed; exact ruler days and contested 1832/1840 capital relocation excluded.

sources.institution: UK Foreign Office / US Department of State Office of the Historian
sources.title: FRUS1890 doc292 — original London Gazette protectorate notice
sources.usage: Read full original correspondence and enclosed 4 November 1890 Gazette: Sultan domains placed under British protectorate, territorial exceptions specified. Conflicting archival guide 1891 date rejected. Protectorate is not annexation or equal rule over all eastern African territories.

sources.institution: Library of Congress Federal Research Division, historical Country Study (HTML transcription)
sources.title: Sudan — Funj and Sennar political order
sources.usage: Read all body paragraphs: confederation under mek/sultan, hereditary viziers and 1761 coup relegating sultan to figurehead, decline into early nineteenth century. Peak seventeenth-century central powers not retrojected into 1800; ethnic community not given political dossier.

sources.institution: Cambridge University Press / Ian Cunnison
sources.title: Kazembe and the Portuguese 1798–1832, original opening extract
sources.usage: Read original opening body extract at lines453–455 (article p61) and detailed reference notes, not merely search snippet: Kazembe eastern monarchy/suzerainty during 1760–1860 and earlier Luapula capital. Only narrow 1815 kingship proposed; inaccessible remaining article not claimed read; ruler chronology/adviser powers/Portuguese titles omitted.

historicalCautions: All intervals are editorial partial cores; exclusive endpoints do not assert complete historical lifetimes.
Era of Princes Ethiopia has nominal imperial identity but fragmented practical authority.
Italian occupation is not consensual or universally recognised annexation; initial 1936 government count is not projected into 1938.
No duplicate Eritrea framework: existing integrated Eritrea entities inspected, but none substituted for occupied Ethiopia or Somaliland component governments. Existing primary source ID reused.
Somali military administrations were separate; Greater Somalia claims do not create unified political control.
Somalia1815 generic identity and HarerEgypt1900 remain unmapped reviewed gaps.
Tanzania prerequisite remains mapping-review: pre1964 United Republic label not mapped onto a mainland-only dependency or combined with Zanzibar by geometry.
British protectorate Zanzibar begins in original1890 Gazette, not archival guide1891 simplification.
Tanganyika council chronology in archival guide is questionable and not accepted; no Tanganyika entity mapped solely through the Tanzania prerequisite.
Kenya1920 and Buganda1900 conservative posttransition cores intentionally use requested1921/1901 with earlier selectable seeds.
1960 Ethiopian coup interval 13–17December omitted explicitly; no uninterrupted imperial administration assumed.
1900Zanzibar protected monarchy distinct from early Omani dependency and later direct British administration.
Community/people identities receive no automatic political dossiers.

Post-return emperor and imperial institutions resume the same revised1955 constitutional framework; no new constitution or permanent polity replacement is asserted. Preserve13–17December1960 as explicitly unresolved coup interruption; earlier and later facts/mappings remain separate.

coordinatorReconciliation.summary: Five duplicate same-framework pairs reconciled. All source-backed fact intervals and mapping/case seed dates retained. No gaps filled; distinct colonial,constitutional andoccupation frameworks not merged.

frameworkWording.note: Names use one revised1955framework label; post-return politicalStatus/governments reuse earlier constitutional values. Dated source-backed intervals/sourceIds/descriptions and13–17Dec1960gap unchanged. Emperor restoration is narrative, not a new constitution.

scope.title: East Africa and Horn
scope.sourceStrategy: Local archives and historical administrative publications; different names and authority fields do not prove succession.
scope.priorityRationale: Early source-family batches prioritise long snapshot presence, broad period potential and national archival/constitutional collections. Source availability is a planning expectation, not an entity-by-entity research finding. Families remain indivisible; no periods are researched now.

difficultCases.question: Review historical-name variants, colonies/occupations and labels such as Tanzania in earlier snapshots; explicit dates need later research.
